title: Chan Chan (Tschudi citadel)
summary: Chan Chan, near Trujillo on Peru's north coast, was the capital of the Chimú kingdom and the largest adobe city of pre-Columbian America. Nine walled 'citadels' or palaces stand in its six-square-kilometre monumental zone; the Tschudi palace is enclosed by an adobe wall about 10 m high. The kingdom peaked in the 15th century.

uncertainty.note: ICOMOS says the Chimú kingdom reached its zenith in the 15th century, shortly before the Inca conquest around 1470. The city is older and Tschudi's own building dates are not given in the sources opened, so 1400 is a nominal start with a wide minus range. End is the present: the ruins stand.

phases.description: The Chimú kingdom reached its zenith in the 15th century; Tschudi is among the later citadels. Exact dates of its construction are not in the sources opened.
After the Inca conquest (about 1470) the city continued until the Spanish founded Trujillo in 1535; the site was afterwards quickly abandoned.
Abandoned after 1535; the adobe is eroding rapidly and the ruins were plundered.

materials.material: unbaked adobe bricks of clay and straw, laid as thick earthen walls

reviewer_note: Shape wall: height and base thickness are the only dimensions with sources, and there is no length for the Tschudi enclosure, so the viewer should draw the wall section only. Heights in other sources run from 7.5 to 18 m; 10 m is CyArk's and the low end of Correo's range, and the base width comes from a newspaper. Least sure of all measurements and of the nominal 1400 start.
